File serving helper procs

Static file metadata cache.

A request that serves a static file normally pays 8-10 stat syscalls (existence check, file info, precompressed variant probes, and one symlink probe per path component). For an unchanged file those results are identical, so we cache them per absolute content path for a short TTL. Serving a hot file then costs at most one full metadata pass per TTL window instead of per request.

Security tradeoff (documented, TTL-bounded): a symlink planted inside the trusted root after a cache entry was populated is not detected for up to the TTL (2 s). Path traversal, root escape, and '..' components are still rejected on every request because validation happens before the cache lookup.

Cheap cache for expandFilename: std/os normalizes paths with heavy allocations (pathnorm), which dominated the static hot path (9.9M calls for ~10 paths). Keyed by input spelling; bounded; process-wide.stat without std/os path normalization (fileExists/getFileInfo each pay a full normalizePath, ~1.2 us, per call). Raw syscall; no string work.Returns the MIME type for a filename based on its extension, defaulting to application/octet-stream.Sends a file with content type, ETag, Last-Modified, range request, and precompressed variant support. Slow tail of sendFile: per-request header building and the rare branches (range requests, 304/HEAD, non-sendfile fallbacks). Kept async so the steady-state path stays a plain synchronous proc (no future allocation, no async dispatch) in the hot loop.Async public API: runs the synchronous core and, only when the fast path did not finish the response, the async slow tail (range/304/HEAD/fallback).Synchronous route handler: zero async machinery on the steady-state path. Plain GET on a cached file is answered entirely synchronously via the sendfile fast path; everything else is delegated to the async slow tail.
